To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we designed a compact X band highly efficient power amplifier in SiGe with 51.7 % peak PAE.
we have demonstrated a compact quasi inverse Class F highly efficient power amplifer (PA) based 130 nm Si Ge technology.
a quasi inverse class F X band highly efficient power amplifier based on 130 nm Si technology is presented.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new design of a high power amplifier for the X band with a good linearity.
the design, simulation, and measurement of the performance of a high power, high efficiency, and linear X band power amplifier in the SiGe process.
the development of a highly efficient and low distortion PA for X band.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed PA is the most efficient SiGe power amplifier reported to date.
this PA exhibits a very high PAE, which is the highest reported so far for a Si based PA in the X band.
this paper presents the first X band highly efficient PA based on SiGe technology, and it is the most efficient Si based X band PA reported so far.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this paper presents the first SiGe X band power amplifier which is highly efficient and linear at the same time.
this paper shows the highest PAE for a X band power amplifier in a Si based technology.
the quasi inverse class F topology is the most efficient topology in SiGe for X band power amplifier.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a low base impedance and a quasi inverse class F load network allows to obtain a high efficiency PA with a good linearity.
a high efficiency PA can be achieved in a small SiGe technology with a simple design.
the proposed PA can be used in high power applications, such as radars, where high efficiency is required.
